proposals.title: One deep-reasoning answer after leaving the paywall
proposals.trigger: After the user opens the Deep reasoning paywall and closes it, show a proposed optional offer back in the Luzia chat.
proposals.userNeed: The user has a question but has not tried a deeper answer. One answer could demonstrate the benefit before they decide whether to subscribe.
proposals.eligibility: Non-subscribers who close this paywall; at most one sample per account, subject to ad availability. Both restrictions are proposed.
proposals.productChange: Add a one-use deep-reasoning answer after paywall dismissal. Do not change the paywall, its normal exit, or the paid entitlement.
proposals.reward: One deep-reasoning answer to the user's next chat question, not continuing access to advanced reasoning or other Luzia+ benefits.
proposals.optIn: On the returned chat, the user explicitly taps Watch ad and completes the ad before choosing to use the sample.
proposals.fulfillment: Mark one subsequent question for deep reasoning, deliver its answer, and then remove the sample badge.
proposals.declinePath: Dismiss the offer and continue the ordinary chat; the subscription offer remains available through its existing path.
proposals.failurePath: If no ad is available or it is unfinished, grant nothing; keep the question available for normal chat and allow the user to leave.
proposals.businessImpact: May improve understanding of Luzia+ and later subscription conversion, but could substitute for a trial or paid reasoning use. Normal chat stays available. Ad revenue and reasoning-compute costs are unknown.
proposals.validationPlan: Randomize eligible paywall closers to this offer or the unchanged return to chat; compare trial starts, paid conversion, retention, normal-chat use, ad completion, and net revenue after compute costs.
assumptions: The observed Deep reasoning control corresponds to the paywall's Advanced reasoning mode benefit.
A single deep-reasoning answer can be granted and accounted for separately.
Ad fill, reasoning cost, conversion, and net revenue are unknown.

proposals.title: An optional alternate draft for a generated app
proposals.trigger: After a user generates an app and sees its ready card on Explore, offer one optional alternate draft for that same idea.
proposals.userNeed: The user wants to assess whether the generated app matches their idea. A second version offers a concrete comparison without replacing the first.
proposals.eligibility: Users with a newly generated, accessible draft; at most one ad-funded alternate per draft. These are proposed rules.
proposals.productChange: Add alternate-draft generation and a way to open either version. Keep the original draft and existing creation flow unchanged; no observed creation limit is asserted.
proposals.reward: One additional generated draft based on the same app idea, with the original retained.
proposals.optIn: The user opens the offer and explicitly chooses to watch and complete an ad before requesting the alternate.
proposals.fulfillment: Generate the alternate draft, add it alongside the original, and let the user open either one.
proposals.declinePath: Dismiss the offer and open or edit the original generated app as before.
proposals.failurePath: If an ad is unavailable or unfinished, do not generate the alternate; leave the original ready card and normal controls usable.
proposals.businessImpact: May increase useful creations and retention, but adds generation and storage costs and could displace ordinary editing. No paid app-creation benefit was observed, so subscription effects are uncertain; do not impose a new limit on normal creation.
proposals.validationPlan: Randomize newly generated drafts to the offer or unchanged ready card; compare draft opens, edits, publishing, retention, subscription conversion, ad revenue, and incremental generation and storage costs.
assumptions: The product can retain and display two drafts for one idea.
Alternate-generation grantability, pricing relationships, service costs, and business metrics are unknown.
No existing app-generation quota or paid creation entitlement was established by these observations.
